News.title: Megxit brought racism rows & cruel ‘villain’ comments, now it’s time for REGREXIT – why I fear the worst is yet to come
News.content:
FIRST we had all the brouhaha about Megxit, followed by six long years of Harry and Meghan cashing in with claims they were bullied and abused royals.

Now, with The Sun breaking the story yesterday that Harry and Meghan are coming home, it seems the ‘American Dream’ is over.





Despite declaring they’d never return to dangerous Britain, it has all gone pear-shaped in LA – so for our next new chapter we’ve got REGREXIT.

But surely before Harry and Megs get out the party streamers and ‘Welcome Home’ banners for themselves – Harry owes his poor pa a very public apology?

Not a phone call, not a private word over tea at Highgrove. Public. Said where the country that mourned Elizabeth II can hear it.

Let’s not forget, just three months after her late Majesty’s state funeral, Netflix released scathing documentary, Harry & Meghan.

He took his ‘freedom flight’ with glee – heading for his American Dream.

They cashed-in big time by betraying confidences. Who can forget Meg’s mock bow, timed for the Christmas ratings?

Harry sat beside her and said nothing.

Add to that the racism claims on Oprah, and the alleged ‘fight night’ with Wills and smashed dog bowl in Spare, the pair have trashed the Queen’s legacy.





There is another debt.

In Spare, Harry called Queen Camilla “the villain,” said she was “dangerous,” and accused her of leaking his own private conversations to rehabilitate her image.

He talked of “bodies left in the street” – his over-the-top expression.

He wrote that she had “sacrificed” him “on her personal PR altar.”

It is an accusation of calculated betrayal, in hardback, against a woman who is now his Queen.

Camilla kept quiet. She didn’t even ask for a correction.

The debt to his brother William hasn’t been paid either.

Now the Palace, commentators, the couple’s own people PR man/team have got to manage this homecoming.



Saying it is a “New chapter” is not enough. More marketing.

But here’s what should worry the palace courtiers charged with keeping the monarchy on track.

That isn’t a couple in crisis reaching for privacy. It looks to me a couple in crisis reaching for a production deal.

They leave California before the end of the month for a private house outside London, possibly the Cotswolds where they stayed during their recent UK visit.

Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, start at a British school in September.

Come on that hasn’t just happened.

That decision has surely been a long time in the planning. They didn’t just pluck it out of the air this weekend.

They are keeping Montecito and their villa in Portugal too.



We are told nothing changes in their status.

Private individuals, non-working royals, no duties resumed.

But if the King thinks they are not going to rock the boat he is wrong, and I fear the worst is yet to come.

If the King was apparently only told on Sunday, he has been seriously blindsided.

It’s very unlikely you could enrol two children in British schools in a fortnight.

There are registrars, headteachers, months of quiet groundwork behind it.

This must have been in the planning for months, and the king is not told?

The sequencing suggests Grandpa was only told once it was unmovable.



They were at Highgrove in July. Charles met Archie and Lilibet for the first time since 2022.

The Palace called it a private family occasion. Reports say it was not discussed. Really?

Now the King has to deal with the fall-out from this fait accompli.

The Palace had no room to soften it before the public had already made up its mind.

On May 2 last year Harry told the BBC he could not see a world in which he would bring his wife and children back to Britain.

He had just lost his appeal over police protection after he sued his father’s government.

MYSTERY OF NEW HOME PRINCE Harry and Meghan will not be moving into a royal residence and instead have lined up a private home. The location has been kept under wraps but there are a number of options. The Cotswolds is popular with American celebrities and A listers who want to live discreetly, and it is near to the King’s Highgrove Estate. Former talk show host Ellen Degeneres had a property there and was friends with Meghan in California. But Prince Harry may want to be close to his mother Princess Diana’s childhood home at Althorp House in Northants where her grave is.

Fifteen months on, the places are booked.

The Home Office answers the security question today much as it answered it then.

Prince Archie is sixth in line to the throne, his dad, fifth.



Until September he is an American boy with a British title, thousands of miles from the institution theoretically he could be asked to serve.

From September he is a child in a British classroom, with British friends, his Californian twang disappearing with every term.

Monarchy runs on familiarity.

It survives on people the country has watched grow up, on faces it knows before it knows anything else about them.

Harry spent six years arguing his kids could not safely have that in dangerous Britain.

Now, despite nothing changing here, he thinks they can.

And still, by every visible sign, he and Meg now want this too.

By welcoming this without demanding the apology first, Charles is creating a problem for himself.

It will leave William holding a bill his father left.

He has spent years building something legible – steady, unshowy – precisely because the family’s alternative default, for a generation now, is chaos dressed up as candour.



Let this pass without an apology and the lesson written into it is plain: grievance, monetised loudly enough and long enough, eventually earns just an institutional shrug.

That is the opposite of everything William’s model of monarchy is meant to prove; restraint gets rewarded, hard work is respected, that the family’s dignity outweighs any one member’s personal whims.

Then there is a question of trust. Can the royals – can we – really trust Meghan and Harry?

Remember even before they let the cat out the bag that they were heading for ‘Freedom” they were filming their grievances, ready to cash in on it down the line.

He had likely been planning his bestseller too.

It is a dilemma for Charles and William. Rise above it, say nothing, and the silence gets read as consent. Bring Harry inside the tent and you are back where you started. Keep him outside and he is free to build what he likes on British soil. There is no clean answer.

Then there are the diaries. Harry and Meghan will have their own engagements here now. Private ones. Commercial ones. Some will fall on the same day as the King’s, or William and Catherine’s. The cameras will have to choose. That is how you end up with an alternative royal family. A headache for the courtiers who plan the year out in advance.

Surely, the Palace should issue a statement – on the record – not whispered advice – reminding the people that the King is sticking to the Sandringham Summit deal.



There will be no half in, half out deal. The Sussexes are private individuals and no taxpayers’ money will be spent on them.

Say it plainly. Before the school gates. Before the Christmas photograph. Harry stands up and says what was done, to whom, and that he’s sorry.

Everything else is fudge.

Robert Jobson is the author of ‘The Windsor Legacy’

News.title: Nato jet destroys drone ‘loaded with explosives’ metres from Black Sea gas project as ‘irresponsible’ Russia slammed
News.content:
DRONE BLASTED Nato jet destroys drone ‘loaded with explosives’ metres from Black Sea gas project as ‘irresponsible’ Russia slammed

NATO scrambled fighter jets to destroy a marine drone reportedly loaded with explosives spotted close to a crucial Black Sea gas project.

Romania spotted the threat around Neptun Deep and quickly sent out F-16 jets to blast away the drone as officials accused Russia of being behind the dangerous act.



The drone got within a few hundred meters from the platform before it was targeted.

Defence Minister Radu Miruta said they had no choice but to intercept the drone “in order to protect the lives of the several hundred people working on the platform”.



The huge Neptun Deep project is expected to make Romania the European Union’s largest gas producer when it comes onstream in 2027.

The offshore site is feared to have become a target due to its vital future role in global gas trade which has been severely hampered since the Ukraine war.

Earlier this month, Romanian army divers were also deployed to destroy two Gerbera-type drones drifting in the exclusive economic zone near the project.

Huge explosions were seen on the water as the drones were blasted with debris sent flying through the air.

Miruta didn’t say who he believed was behind the maritime scare but did confirm Ukraine said it wasn’t associate with their forces.

Romanian President Nicusor Dan quickly blamed Russia for today’s intrusion.



He said: “I strongly condemn the intensification of these types of irresponsible incidents on the part of the Russian Federation.

“We remain vigilant alongside Nato allies to defend ourselves and repel such challenges.”

Nato states Romania, Bulgaria and Turkey have neutralised more than 150 mines drifting across trade lanes in the Black Sea in recent years.



The three states have now agreed to expand a joint task force that patrols the water clearing mines to now include missions to protect critical infrastructure.

Neptun Deep is jointly owned by OMV Petrom and state gas producer Romgaz.

Romania shares a 382-mile land border with Ukraine and has seen Russian drones breaching its airspace over the last four years of war.

The latest came overnight when a drone entered Romanian airspace near Galati before crashing in an unpopulated area in the country of Tulcea.

Two Spanish F-18 aircraft and a Romanian helicopter were later deployed to protect the border.



A raging European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen slammed a “hybrid warfare” campaign against the bloc earlier today.

She said: “An escalating campaign of threats is underway, unsettling our citizens and seeking to divide our Union.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Von der Leyen warned the EU must step up its defence plans to be able to “deter provocation and aggression”.

She fell short of directly blaming Vladimir Putin’s Russia.

News.title: Tinder swindler who stole £70k from women by claiming he was ex-special forces multi-millionaire with cancer is jailed
News.content:
CROOK CAGED Tinder swindler who stole £70k from women by claiming he was ex-special forces multi-millionaire with cancer is jailed

A TINDLER swindler who stole £70,000 from women after claiming he was a multi-millionaire with cancer has been jailed.

Joseph Gibson, 35, lied about serving in the Special Boat Service and pretended he owned luxury yachts and cars.



The scammer, who claimed he was worth £400million, also claimed he had cancer and sent photos apparently sent from his hospital bed.

Gibson has now been jailed for three years and two months after admitting four counts of fraud.



Bristol Crown Court heard he conned three women and one man out of £68,000 between July 2020 and October 2021.

Lying Gibson met two of his victims on Tinder and convinced one of them they were in a relationship.

He told the women he had cancer, previously served in the Special Boat Service and had been blown up by an improvised explosive device (IED).

But his lies, which included sending pictures of large houses he said he was buying, were dismissed as “total fantasy”.



His first victim, a Devon-based businesswoman, lost more than £5,200 after believing his lies and handed over money for him to purchase stock for her retail business.

In August 2020, Gibson told the victim he had cancer and even sent her a photograph of himself purportedly in a hospital bed.

By the end of his fraud, the woman had just 93p left in her bank account.



Gibson’s second victim – described as “another Tinder trap” – was targeted by the conman when he discovered she had £10,000 in a savings account.

The crook based himself on Mr Grey from the Fifty Shades Of Grey film and convinced the woman to send him her money so he could turn it into £150,000.

In 2021, she took out a £4,000 loan after Gibson claimed he urgently needed money for private cancer treatment.

The woman was later forced to take out an individual voluntary agreement to manage her debts.

Gibson’s third victim – a relative of the second woman – took out loans to invest in his bogus investment deals but lost more than £18,000.



The final victim was a retired superyacht captain who dreamed of travelling around the world with his wife.

Gibson told him he had purchased a £7million yacht after selling a weapons programme to the US government for £400million.

In total, the man gave Gibson more than £25,000 to invest in his businesses, the court heard.



Even after he was snared, the criminal continued to spread a web of lies and previously begged a judge to hold off on his sentencing.

Gibson claimed he he had £40,000 in savings to repay his victims after working in the engineering industry in the UK, Bulgaria and Dubai.

The court heard today he was unable to raise the sum and could only provide £15,000 until more funds became available.

He told Recorder Jaron Crooknorth that he could save £5,000 per month for compensation and asked for his sentence to be deferred for a further nine months to fully repay his victims.

But the judge refused his request and also ordered the start of proceedings to recover money gained through his fraud.



He told Gibson: “Joseph Gibson, you are simply a fraudster.

“It has taken years for you to admit that.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Pity those who have had the misfortune to have you come into their lives, prey on their affections, steal their money, steal their goals and fracture their relationships.”

Gibson will next appear for a hearing under the Proceeds of Crime Act, to recover his assets to repay his victims, in March.

News.title: Migrant, 19, confesses to stabbing colleague, 42, to death in ‘brutal, unspeakable way’ after ‘intimate’ relationship
News.content:
AN ILLEGAL immigrant has allegedly confessed to brutally stabbing his colleague to death in an “unspeakable” way after an “intimate” relationship.

Alexis Cedillos-Campos, from El Salvador, 19, was arrested for killing 42-year-old Carmen Lizet Puch in a car park 15 miles outside of Washington DC.



Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis said the pair worked together at Bitez restaurant – a halal-eatery in Herndon, Virginia – and shared an “intimate relationship”.

Carmen, described as a “loving mum to her 3-year-old girl,” was found drenched in petrol with multiple stab wounds near the Difficult Run Park trail in Great Falls.



“Our victim suffered numerous stab wounds in a really brutal, unspeakable way,” said Davis.

Detectives are still working to piece together the full picture, including whether other relationships played a part in the killing.



Davis said: “We also know that our killer left the restaurant on the night of the murder with a fixed-blade knife.”

He said that police have CCTV of Cedillos-Campos taking the knife, a pair of black latex gloves and a water bottle “with the intent to do harm and kill the victim”.

The chief added that it was “all very premeditated”.

Cedillos-Campos then allegedly siphoned petrol from a motorbike and filled the water bottle.



After stabbing Carmen “repeatedly”, he failed to set her body alight.

Davis said: “The way that she was treated by this killer was reprehensible.”

A jogger discovered Carmen’s body lying next to her 2011 Honda Civic in a small gravel car park at around 6.45am on Monday before calling 911.



Cedillos-Campos was arrested in Maryland on Wednesday morning and is awaiting extradition to Virginia.

Davis said that the suspect confessed to the killing and was cooperating with the investigation.

Cedillos-Campos was snared by Border Patrol agents in April 2024 after he illegally crossed into the US near El Paso, Texas.

He was taken into custody by Customs and Border Protection but later released.

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said: “Biden and Mayorkas hand-delivered alleged killer Cedillos-Campos to the streets of Fairfax County.



“They recklessly unleashed millions of unvetted illegal aliens into American communities and abused the law to do so.”

Davis said detectives are now interviewing witnesses, friends, family and coworkers.

He added that Cedillos-Campos’s “immigration status plays no role in how they conduct their investigations”.

Bitez owner Abdul Anwari told NBC Washington: “I don’t know if you can process something like this.

“It’s not something you expect. It’s not something that anyone would ever want to happen.



“But you know, we’re still taking it minute at a time.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Carmen’s daughter is now being cared for by her family.

Anwari has set up a GoFundMe to help cover Carmen’s funeral costs and provide some money for her daughter.

News.title: The terrifying ‘Lucky Dip’ car theft craze coming to Britain’s streets after 5 teens killed in wrong-way motorway smash
News.content:
IT was only a matter of time before the “Lucky Dip” gangsters caused death and misery.

Some of the five teenagers who died in a head on crash in Ireland on Sunday had posted clips of themselves being pursued by blue lights as loud music blared.





They uploaded videos weaving in and out of traffic, with one including the caption “wrong way”.

Now a family-of-four are in hospital, some of them fighting for their lives after the BMW containing the five balaclava youngsters piled into them going up the M9 motorway in County Kildare in the wrong direction.

Alma and Niamh Kinsella, Ellie Hendricken and a seven-year-old boy were heading to a wedding when they were hit by the five ‘joy riders’.

Joey Carthy, 15, Alex McCarthy, Jack Kennedy, Kamil Pustkowski, all aged 17, and 18-year-old Jeremy O’Brien all died in the BMW.

Some of them had written Lucky Dip Gang into their social media profiles.

This is a gang that has been terrorising Ireland.

Fluid but well organised, gangsters pick an area at random, break into properties and steal cars and cause mayhem.

The lives cut short in the early hours of Sunday morning is not going to deter others, an expert warns.





It is feared the balaclava clad Lucky Dip gang could become a social media trend that spreads to the United Kingdom.

Retired Scotland Yard DCI Mick Neville tells The Sun: “Social media is such that people in England will think ‘that’s a good idea, we’ll have a go at that as well’.

“It’s a contagion, so I’ve no doubts that some idiots somewhere are thinking we’ll have a go at that.

“For the criminals they get to pass their tips on how to do it, and they get the bravado effect of people liking it.”

Their reckless disregard for the life of other road users is a major headache for police forces.

It is too dangerous for police pursuit teams to go after a car which is heading the wrong way up a motorway.



That could cause other vehicles to swerve and crash.

Mick says: “You’ve got to close the motorway. That’s the safest way to do that.”

The Garda had opted not to pursue the BMW going the wrong way up the M9 on Sunday, planning instead to stop the vehicle with a stinger device at the next junction.

But the five crashed before they got there.

There were reports of similarly risky driving videos appearing on the social media site TikTok.

The company insists they have now removed this content.

That is unlikely to stop teens bragging about their dangerous driving by sharing clips.

Petrolheads regularly race each other on Britain’s roads, often posting videos of 100mph plus speeds and illegal manoeuvres.



But all is not lost.

Social media can provide crucial clues to detectives.

Whenever a car thief or joy rider uploads an image of themselves committing an offence they provide the police with important evidence.

The so-called Bally Boys – named after their balaclavas – believe that because they don’t show their faces there isn’t a case.

Mick, though, insists you can identify a suspect who is wearing a balaclava.

The ex-head of Forensic Imaging at the Met Police is now CEO at Super Recognisers International.

They help police forces across Europe to train police officers to identify criminals caught on CCTV and other digital imagery.

Mick explains: “You can identify people in balaclavas, just by looking at their eyes. From a police point of view, you’ve got some real good evidence there.”

The super recognisers are trained to see one aspect of an image, such as the eyes or an item of clothing, and then to link them to a previous offence.

By building up a jigsaw of information detectives can identify the criminal.



Mick continues: “If you get a name, then you start looking for the balaclava and get the DNA, don’t you?

“You get the branded clothing that they’re wearing in the car. With a name, you can start to track people. You can look at their phones and see where they were at a particular time.”

That means that social media can be useful.

Mick adds: “It’s a double-edged sword, really. I mean, I’ve had a few convictions off social media.

“Like when a young lad was robbed in Streatham and he said, ‘I don’t know the bloke’s name, but I know he’s in some of these drill rap videos.’

“We extracted the image and got it ID’d. If you’re going to be mug enough to put yourself on social media, then the police can get you.”

Super recognisers are already being used by Hertfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Thames Valley police and by German forces.

Mick had been in touch with the Irish Garda prior to the recent tragedy.



He thinks the quicker the police catch these criminals the better.

Putting the Lucky Dip gang and their ilk behind bars is a good way to prevent more copycats.

Two of the teens who died in the BMW smash on Sunday were linked to another road accident last month.

Both Carthy and McCarthy were questioned by Gardai over a hit-and-run in Carlow.

What Mick wants to see is police forces being more proactive, getting on top of social media-inspired criminals before they get out of hand.

He concludes: “They’re not using the technology in a smart way at the moment.”

News.title: Husband and wife who died when light aircraft crashed are pictured after ‘challenging search operation’ in countryside
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH TRAGEDY Husband and wife who died when light aircraft crashed are pictured after ‘challenging search operation’ in countryside

THE husband and wife killed in a horror plane crash last week have been pictured as tributes to the couple flood in.

Ketan Swali, 59, and Sheetal Swali, 55, were supposed to land at an airport in North Wales on August 14 but failed to appear.



Ketan, member of a Staffordshire flying club, was remembered as being “popular”.

The club said in an online tribute: “Ketan was a very popular member and loved to talk about flying and aviation.



“Our heartfelt condolences go to their families and friends at this difficult time.”

Police were called to the scene at Caernarfon Airport at around midday before launching a multi-agency search for the light aircraft.



It was shortly afterwards found in a remote area near Trawsfynydd, Gwynedd where the two, both from Syston in Leicestershire, were pronounced dead.

A team of investigators from the Air Accidents Investigations Branch (AAIB) shortly after launched a probe into the tragedy.



The cause of death has provisionally been identified as major impact trauma.

Ch Supt Owain Llewellyn said: “Our thoughts are with the families and friends of those involved in this tragic incident.

“We will support the AAIB with their investigation to ensure the circumstances leading to this incident are fully understood.

“This has been a challenging search operation and I am grateful to all of the agencies involved for their professionalism and dedication.”

The plane has been travelling from Tatenhill Airport in Burton-upon-Trent in a Piper PA28 plane.



North Wales Police are supporting the AAIB in its probe into the tragedy.

The two HGVs collided this morning on the clockwise carriageway between Junction 5 and Junction 6 at Godstone, Surrey.

News.title: Will there be a UK heatwave on the August 2026 bank holiday? Latest Met Office weather forecast
News.content:
WITH the August Bank Holiday a week away, Brits planning beer garden outings, coastal trips, or festival visits are keeping a close eye on the forecast.

Following mid-August’s blistering temperatures, the latest Met Office updates show that something of a meteorological shift is underway.



That could make a Bank Holiday heatwave unlikely, but the upcoming long weekend still looks set to offer some optimism for those with plans outdoors.

At the time of writing, the Met Office’s latest blog says that “after weeks of predominantly hot and dry weather,” the pattern across the UK has shifted.



That has brought with it “a very different feel“, with a “noticeable drop in temperatures.”

While early August brought scorching conditions, low pressure systems have broken the extreme heat, ushering in fresher, wetter conditions across many regions.

What is the forecast for the August Bank Holiday?

Looking ahead to the three-day weekend across August 29-31, the Met Office’s long-range forecast predicts a mixed bag.

The week will start on a promising note, with conditions “largely dry and settled” as “a ridge of high pressure continues to extend across the country.”

But forecasters say this calm spell will be brief as the long weekend approaches.

The Met Office says the weather is likely to turn “more unsettled during the week and through to the turn of the month as low pressure becomes more dominant.”



This change in pressure systems is set to bring “showers or longer spells of rain, perhaps heavy, to most if not all areas at times though still some sunny interludes.”

The forecaster adds that conditions could become “possibly windy at times too.”

Will there be a Bank Holiday heatwave?

In the UK, an “official” heatwave is declared when a location meets or exceeds a specific daily maximum temperature threshold for at least three consecutive days.

These thresholds vary by region to account for local climates, ranging from 25C in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, and northern England up to 28C in London and the southeast.

If temperatures fall short of the local benchmark on any of those three days, the spell fails to qualify.



The Met Office’s long-range projection essentially rules out any prolonged extreme heat.

It forecasts that overall temperatures will remain “likely near to average though varying.”

But weather analysts say that there could still be “some short-lived warm and humid spells possible, especially in the south,” offering moments of summer warmth between unsettled weather fronts.

While the Met Office’s long-range computer models provide an idea of the weather ahead of time, the forecast will firm up significantly as meteorologists get within three to five days of the Bank Holiday weekend.

News.title: Students in Liverpool told A-level places have have been cancelled in 'bombshell' update
News.content:
Students in Liverpool told A-level places have have been cancelled in 'bombshell' update

Students expecting to begin A-Levels at City of Liverpool College next month have been told the courses will no longer run.

View 3 Images City of Liverpool College has confirmed it will no longer offer A-Levels to new first-year students. (Image: Liverpool Echo)

Students collecting their GCSE results have been told their planned A-Level places at a Liverpool college have been cancelled just weeks before the new academic year.

‌



City of Liverpool College confirmed it will not offer A-Levels to new first-year students in the 2026-27 academic year. Those already in their second year will be able to complete their courses as planned.

‌



Affected students were informed during enrolment on Thursday with staff understood to have been told of the decision just 24 hours earlier, reports the Liverpool Echo.

‌



A college spokesperson said: "Following an extensive review, we have taken the decision to withdraw our small A-level provision for first year students for the 26-27 Academic year, students on their second year of study will complete their A-levels with us as originally planned."

The decision means young people who had expected to begin A-Levels at the college next month will now have to consider alternative places or other courses.

View 3 Images (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



A staff member, who spoke anonymously to the Echo, described the announcement as a "bombshell". They said: “We've had three open evenings where young people have come from schools across the city, and we've made them an offer of an A-Level place. But now, when they come in to enrol, they'll be told there's no longer any places for them.”

They added: “Instead of preparing for the future they'd planned and had in place, their future has been plunged into uncertainty.

"Some of our students are from disadvantaged backgrounds, who may not have had the grades to get A-Level places in other institutions, but who still wanted to get their A-Levels. What will happen to them now?"

‌



The college said its decision followed a review which considered factors including record growth in student numbers in technical and vocational areas, student capacity, staff wellbeing, falling A-Level applications and the availability of other A-Level providers across Liverpool.

View 3 Images City of Liverpool College has confirmed it will no longer offer A-Levels to new first-year students. (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Officials said staff would be available during enrolment to help affected students explore alternatives, including T-Levels and other qualifications at the college or courses elsewhere in the city.

‌



The spokesperson added: “We're confident that this approach will ensure every student has the opportunity to study their desired subject area.”

Concerns have also been raised among staff who teach A-Levels, including some who were reportedly recruited earlier this year expecting to teach the courses for the next few years.

Staff told the Echo they fear their hours could be reduced, although the college has said there will be no redundancies. Some have also expressed concerns about being redeployed onto courses outside their usual specialisms.

Article continues below

A college source told the Echo that A-Levels would no longer be offered from 2027 onwards, but City of Liverpool College said no decision has been made on its 2027/28 curriculum.

News.title: Son of 'Britain's most evil mum' says his 'childhood was taken'
News.content:
Son of 'Britain's most evil mum' says his 'childhood was taken'

Matthew Johnson has spoken about the lasting impact on his childhood after his mother spent years falsely claiming he was seriously ill and subjecting him to unnecessary medical treatment

View 4 Images Matthew has opened up on his feelings after years of false illness claims made by his mother (Image: Ken McKay/ITV/Shutterstock)

A man whose mum was jailed for faking his illnesses has told how his childhood was taken from him.

‌



Matthew Johnson, 25, was subjected to years of unnecessary medical treatment as a young child after his mother Lisa Hayden-Johnson falsely claimed he was seriously ill and unable to walk, eat or breathe without help. She was jailed in 2010 for three years and three months after admitting cruelty and perverting the course of justice.

‌



Now Matthew has spoken about the lasting impact of what happened to him. He told the BBC: “I do think that my childhood was taken from me and that’s something that you can’t go back to, so it is difficult to process.”

‌



View 4 Images Hayden-Johnson said she was putting her son first (Image: Brad Wakefield / SWNS.COM)

His story is being revisited in documentary Love You To Death, which also features medics from NHS Torbay, social workers, Devon police and his mother. In the first episode, which aired on Wednesday (August 19), Hayden-Johnson rejected the ‘most evil mum’ label used in coverage of the case.

She said: “I’ve never had the opportunity to [tell her story]. The newspaper articles are so incorrect. How can I be ‘Britain’s Most Evil Mother?’ The only thing I was guilty of was putting my son first and fighting his battle, which is what I did. And I don’t regret that.”

‌



But Matthew said hearing his mother’s comments confirmed he had made the right decision to cut ties with her. He has not been in touch with Hayden-Johnson for two years and said it “puts it to rest that I’ve made the right decision for me and my future”.

Matthew was born prematurely and initially needed medical support before making a full recovery. But for the next six years his mother continued to insist he was seriously unwell. She claimed he suffered from a string of conditions including diabetes, food allergies, cerebral palsy and cystic fibrosis, as well as saying he was allergic to sunlight.

View 4 Images Lisa successfully nominated him for a Child of Courage award (Image: Alamy Stock Photo)

‌



Matthew visited doctors and hospitals hundreds of times and underwent invasive medical procedures and treatment for illnesses he did not have. He was also made to use mobility aids including a wheelchair and carry oxygen. Looking back, he said he did not remember feeling unwell but had “quite of lot of medication” and even underwent surgery.

He said: “It feels that so many things were declared wrong with me, it was hard to identify with one of them.”

He said his mother said he had difficulty breathing, and added: “There were times she said I was damaged by sunlight and had to wear special glasses and when I needed mobility support, whether a stroller a walker or a wheelchair”.

‌



He said the illnesses he was said to have “seemed contradictory” and "It felt like a trail of different ones, there wasn’t anything that seemed permanent.”

The claims surrounding Matthew’s health also brought him significant public attention. He appeared on television and met high-profile figures including then-prime minister Tony Blair and the then Duchess of Cornwall, now Queen Camilla.

View 4 Images A young Matthew with his mum (Image: TNA)

‌



His mother successfully nominated him for a Children of Courage award while also claiming around £20,000 a year in benefits and receiving free holidays including cruises. But doctors eventually became suspicious about Matthew’s symptoms and he was due to attend a hospital assessment.

To avoid the appointment, Hayden-Johnson falsely told police she had been sexually assaulted and was reported to have injured herself to create physical evidence for the claim.

Police later found holiday footage showing Matthew running around in swimming trunks on a cruise despite the serious health and mobility problems his mother had claimed he suffered from which later led to her imprisonment for child cruelty and perverting the course of justice for falsely claiming she was sexually assaulted.

Article continues below

Taking part in Love You To Death, Matthew has said he learned more about his childhood he struggled to understand prior. He told the BBC: “You can’t really fathom it, it’s a really difficult thing to explain, It’s such an extraordinary situation, I think it definitely impacted me, it’s such a key stage of development.”

As he grew older, relatives were careful about the information they told him, he said: “They didn’t want to tell me too early to take me away from the normal life that I was living, but also they didn’t want to tell me at a point where I wouldn’t fully understand.”

He said he processed what happened to him “from things that I had read, from things that people had told me,” adding: “I’ve just got on with what I’ve been doing. I’ve looked ahead and didn’t want to seek the past because it’s not a place that I want to visit. So I’ve always just cracked on with what I want to do for the future.”

News.title: NHS transplant landmark sees turbo charged lungs ‘breathe’ outside of body
News.content:
NHS transplant landmark sees turbo charged lungs ‘breathe’ outside of body

WARNING: GRAPHIC IMAGES First lungs transplanted in world-leading pilot after they were pumped with oxygenated blood and nutrients - an NHS change which could save hundreds of lives a year

NHS delivers UK's first revolutionary ‘three hospital’ transplant

The first lung transplant has been conducted as part of a pioneering NHS scheme to save hundreds of lives.

‌



The complete set of lungs were boosted by pumping them with oxygenated blood and nutrients before being sent to another part of the country and successfully transplanted into a recipient who has since been discharged from hospital.

‌



The NHS is the first health service in the world to implement ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) assessment which is expected to increase usable donor organs by 20%. This would enable extra transplants to save or improve 750 more lives every year.

‌



NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT) has released footage of the lungs “breathing” while hooked up to a machine to be boosted and tested at Royal Papworth Hospital in Cambridge. They were then sent to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham for transplant into a donor on the waiting list.

View 5 Images WARNING GRAPHIC IMAGES: 'Breathing' lungs ready for transplant

Aaron Ranasinghe, consultant lung transplant surgeon at the Queen Elizabeth, said: “This landmark transplant demonstrates what can be achieved when NHS organisations collaborate in new and innovative ways to make the very best use of donated organs.”

‌



View 5 Images Surgeons Marius Berman and Pradeep Kaul observing the lungs

It comes as the NHS transplant waiting list is at a record high with thousands of people waiting and dying before they get an organ. The rate of bereaved families supporting donation has dropped to 59%, down from 68% before the Covid-19 pandemic

Royal Papworth is one of 15 hospitals in England equipped with “perfusion” machines where organs otherwise discarded are boosted and undergo further tests to reassure surgeons they can be transplanted safely. The Mirror last month reported how the very first organ saved and transplanted under the national pilot was a liver.

‌



Health minister Karin Smyth said: “This is a fantastic example of British medical innovation saving lives. I am incredibly proud that the UK is hosting the first national programme of this kind anywhere in the world, giving patients a better chance of a life-changing operation.

View 5 Images Lungs being prepared

“This breakthrough could help save or improve an additional 750 lives every year, and it is a testament to the skill and collaboration of our NHS staff and scientists that the UK is a world leader in this field.”

‌



Currently some donated organs fall into a clinical grey area, where initial assessments do not provide enough information to confidently determine whether they are fit for transplant. Decisions must often be made within a matter of hours so such organs can be declined out of caution.

The 15 new Assessment and Recovery Centres (ARCs) test and boost these organs to give transplant teams more information about organ function before a transplant takes place.

View 5 Images Lungs being perfused

‌



Andrew Fisher, consultant in severe lung disease and NHSBT lead for the ARCs programme, said: “I am delighted that the first lung transplant has been performed using donor lungs that have had their quality checked in an ARC pilot site before being sent to another transplant centre for a patient on their waiting list.

“All transplant teams now have the ability to ask for donor lungs where there is uncertainty if they can be used, to be sent to an ARC to be tested. It shows the potential for this to increase the number of suitable lungs available for transplant and to make lung perfusion technology available to every patient on the waiting lists across the country.

“We should also remember that none of this is possible without the generosity of the donor and all families who support donation. They are lifesavers.”

‌



View 5 Images Mirror campaign achieved historic law change (Image: Daily Mirror)

The Mirror campaigned for Max and Keira’s law in the name of Keira Ball, who died, aged nine, in a car crash, then saved the life of Max Johnson, nine, who received her heart.

The law change which came into force in 2020 and was credited with helping keep organ donation going during the Covid crisis. It meant there would be a presumption in favour of donation but bereaved next of kin would always retain their right to veto transplants. More families have vetoed transplants since the pandemic and the reason for this is unclear.

Article continues below

The NHS states that it is vital that people sign the Organ Donor Register to make their wishes clear, in case the worst happens. Wasting fewer organs is seen as one answer to tackling the record transplant waiting list. In the past decade nearly 5,000 people have died waiting for a life-saving transplant.

To find out more and to register an organ donation decision call 0300 123 23, visit organdonation.nhs.uk or use the NHS app.

News.title: Tinder conman who faked cancer and lied about being soldier left woman with 93p
News.content:
Tinder conman who faked cancer and lied about being soldier left woman with 93p

Joseph Gibson, 35, conned people out of £68,000, after claiming he had served in the Special Boat Service, owned luxury yachts and cars, and was worth £400 million

View 5 Images (Image: Avon and Somerset Police/PA Wire)

A conman who claimed he was a special forces soldier turned multi-millionaire cancer patient and left one of victims with just 93p has been jailed.

‌



Joseph Gibson, 35, lied that he had served in the Special Boat Service, owned luxury yachts and cars, and was worth £400 million.

‌



He was eventually arrested and admitted four counts of fraud, relating to three women and one man, who he conned out of £68,000 between July 2020 and October 2021.

‌



The court heard how Gibson met two of his victims on Tinder and convinced one of them they were in a relationship. His first victim, a Devon-based businesswoman, lost more than £5,200 after believing his lies and handing over money for him to purchase stock for her retail business.

View 5 Images (Image: Avon and Somerset Police/PA Wire)

Pilot dead after Pennsylvania State Police helicopter and small plane crash mid-air READ MORE :

In August 2020, Gibson, of Ruthin, Denbighshire, told the woman that he had cancer and even sent her a photograph of himself purportedly in a hospital bed. By the end of his fraud, the woman had just 93p left in her bank account.

‌



He showed pictures of large houses and claimed he was thinking of buying them. Gibson told his victims that he had cancer, had served in the Special Boat Service, had been blown up by an improvised explosive device (IED) – with the judge describing these claims as “total fantasy”.

In text messages released following the case, Gibson is shown claiming he had homes in Sandbanks, Bath, Dubai, Singapore and Mayfair, London, as well as 21 rental properties.

He wrote: “Mate I have everything I want I have amazing houses cars boats helicopters.” Gibson also claimed to have made £1.1 million through financial trading, adding: “I am trading a 5 million account on my phone from a hospital bed”.

‌



View 5 Images Gibson during his arrest (Image: Metropolitan Police / SWNS)

In one exchange, he asked a victim about their preference for clothing and shoe brands. After being asked the spending limit, Gibson replied: “Haha can I let you into a little secret I think we know you well enough and I can trust you now but please do not repeat it it’s not in a bragging and showing off way I’m pretty humble… In January I was valued at 440m if you need me.”

The judge described Gibson’s second victim as “another Tinder trap” in which he based himself on Mr Grey from the Fifty Shades Of Grey film. Gibson discovered the woman had £10,000 in savings and convinced her to send it to him for investing, claiming he could turn it into £150,000.

‌



In 2021, the woman took out a £4,000 loan as Gibson claimed he urgently needed money for private cancer treatment. She was later forced to take out an individual voluntary agreement to manage her debts. “She is broken and exhausted,” the judge told Gibson. “She has lost all confidence and trust.”

The third victim was a relative of the second victim, and took out loans to invest in Gibson’s bogus investment deals. In total, she lost more than £18,000. “She begged for her money back,” the judge told Gibson.

View 5 Images (Image: Avon and Somerset Police / SWNS)

‌



Gibson’s final victim was a retired superyacht captain, who the defendant told he had purchased a £7 million yacht after selling a weapons programme to the US government for £400 million. The man described how he was driven to tears writing his victim personal statement, describing the impact of Gibson’s offending on him.

“His dream of travelling around the world with his wife has gone,” said the judge, Recorder Jaron Crooknorth.

The fraudster previously asked a judge at Bristol Crown Court to delay sentencing in his case – claiming he had £40,000 in savings to repay his victims after working in the engineering industry in the UK, Bulgaria and Dubai.

‌



On Thursday, Gibson admitted he had been unable to raise the sum and could only provide £15,000 until more funds became available. He told the judge that he could save £5,000 per month for compensation and asked for his sentence to be deferred for a further nine months to fully repay his victims.

However, the Judge Crooknorth refused that request and instead jailed Gibson for three years and two months. The judge also ordered the start of proceedings to recover money gained through his fraud.

View 5 Images Text messages Joseph Gibson sent to one of his victims (Image: Avon and Somerset Police/PA Wire)

‌



“Joseph Gibson, you are simply a fraudster,” the judge told him. “It has taken years for you to admit that. Pity those who have had the misfortune to have you come into their lives, prey on their affections, steal their money, steal their goals and fracture their relationships.”

The judge said Gibson had been of previous good character and admitted his offending, albeit shortly before his trial. He added that the defendant would get “very little” reduction in his sentence for remorse.

“You are sorry for the position you have found yourself in,” the judge said. “You have tried to persuade this court that you have more money than you have. You have not shown evidence of that money to me. You have sought to deceive this court into believing that you had it.”

‌



Gibson appeared to be shaking throughout the court hearing. He will next appear for a hearing under the Proceeds of Crime Act, to recover his assets to repay his victims, in March.

Speaking after the case, lead investigator Jenny Williams, of Avon and Somerset Police, said: “Joseph Gibson is a confident and manipulative man who developed an extensive web of lies for his own personal gain.

“The impact of fraud on victims can often be profound and long-lasting, and those duped by Gibson have been left with significant debt, a loss of trust and the difficult task of rebuilding their lives. His deception has left his victims struggling to come to terms with the extent of his dishonesty.”

News.title: Brits ignoring wearable tech health alerts – and it could be dangerous
News.content:
Brits ignoring wearable tech health alerts – and it could be dangerous

UK adults now track their health using wearable tech such as smartwatches and fitness trackers — but many admit they have no idea what the data means, with some ignoring health alerts entirely.

View 3 Images More than half of Brits own some form of wearable tech (Image: Getty Images)

Nearly half of adults are tracking their health through wearable tech - but a quarter confess they haven't got a clue what they're looking for. A study of 2,000 adults revealed 57% now wear some form of tech which monitors their heart rate, steps, sleep and even blood pressure.

‌



Nearly half (46%) actively track their health and wellbeing via their watch, phone or smart ring. Yet, 23% of those admit they don't understand what most of the information is telling them, with 60% having previously looked at data on their device without knowing what it means.

‌



Meanwhile, 24% have completely ignored health alerts from their device, with heart rate (40%), activity levels (35%), and stress (32%) warnings the most frequently overlooked.

‌



View 3 Images Almost four in ten people struggle to interpret the data from their devices (Image: Getty Images)

The study was commissioned by Cromwell Hospital , which offers cardiology services alongside Bupa’s other hospitals, King Edward VII’s Hospital and New Victoria Hospital.

Dr Neil Srinivasan, consultant cardiologist at Cromwell Hospital, said: "Wearable technology has changed the way people monitor their health. From steps to sleep and heart rate, we now have a wealth of data at our fingertips, people need to know what they are looking out for.

‌



"Worryingly, this lack of understanding is causing some to ignore alerts and signals which could indicate a serious health issue, particularly ones that are linked to our hearts.

"These alerts should not be ignored and should be checked out by a healthcare professional, who will be able to tell you what it means and if more investigations need to happen.

"We know that early diagnosis can be lifesaving. Using all the tools at our disposal, including wearable technology and preventative screenings, is key to maintaining good health particularly for your heart."

‌



The study also revealed that steps taken (67%), heart rate (52%) and calories burned (46%) are the most frequently monitored health metrics via wearable technology.

However, only 17% can interpret the data from their device that may be linked to irregular heart rhythms, and just 21% feel confident in understanding the information relating to their respiratory rate.

View 3 Images Experts warn that health alerts should always be checked out (Image: Getty Images)

‌



When faced with confusing readings from their wearable tech, 61% turn to the internet to find out what it means, while 30% simply disregard it. Worryingly, one in four (26%) admitted that a lack of understanding left them anxious without good reason.

The research, conducted through OnePoll, discovered that 28% of those who monitor their health via wearable tech have sought medical advice following an alert or notification related to their wellbeing.

Of those who did get checked out, 58% found it turned out to be a minor issue, yet 21% said it proved to be an indicator of a more serious health concern.

‌



More than a third (35%) have also shared data from their wearable tech device when consulting a medical professional, with 26% of those believing it resulted in a quicker or more straightforward diagnosis.

As technology continues to open up new ways of monitoring our health, wearable data is increasingly being supported by additional tools that can help people identify the risks of serious illnesses years before any symptoms emerge.

From 1 September 2026, Bupa will launch a new first-to-market genomics prevention-focused pathway for cardiovascular disease.

Article continues below

It will use DNA insights to pinpoint individuals at heightened risk and connect them with preventive services included within their health cover, such as Bupa's Weight Management Plan, to reduce their chances of developing cardiovascular disease in the future.

Dr Srinivasan added: "Technology is allowing us to get far more information about our bodies than ever before, information that previously would only be available from a doctor. "Understanding the data to spot any early warning signs of health concerns that might not be quite as they should be, and get treatment faster, especially when it comes to our heart health. ".
