According to the committee, drainage channels built during the reign of David the Builder stopped functioning in 1510 after Ottoman forces burned the monastery. The committee says archaeological excavations also support this conclusion.

“For centuries, the drainage system was filled with earth, ash and coal,” the committee said.

The committee also responded to criticism over humidity and condensation inside the church. According to the committee, Italian professor Dario Camuffo conducted the study of Gelati’s microclimate. The committee considers him one of the recognised experts in the study of the microclimate of cultural heritage sites.

The committee explained that the problem at Gelati stems from the church’s massive walls, which retain the cold for a long time during winter. In spring, when outdoor temperatures rise and warm air enters the church, condensation can form on the walls and floor.

Camuffo suggested gradually heating the floor as one possible solution. However, the committee stressed that this remains a working hypothesis and requires further research before a final decision.

The committee also clarified the memorandum it signed with the Italian institute Opificio delle Pietre Dure. According to the committee, the “pilot restoration” provided for in the document does not mean conducting experiments at Gelati. Instead, it refers to pilot or trial restoration work, which is standard international practice.

“This is a widely accepted standard for restoring wall paintings. Before treating an entire fresco, conservators test the safety of the proposed conservation methods on a small, less visible area. Only after obtaining a positive result do they begin the full-scale process,” the committee said.

In a significant part of its statement, the committee also responded to critics and addressed allegations about the condition of the mosaics at Gelati.

According to the committee, experts already knew about the poor condition of the mosaics in 1989. The claim is based on an assessment by restorer Carlo Bakuradze at the time, who found that about 85% of the mosaic depicting the Virgin Mary had detached from its base.

The committee also criticised specialists who question the ongoing conservation work and reminded them of their own responsibility for Gelati’s condition in the past.

“It is cynical and hypocritical for people to question the quality of conservation work when, under their direct supervision, extensive water-infiltration problems emerged within just one year at the recently built Bagrati Cathedral — problems that persist to this day,” the statement said. The Temporary Committee for the Rehabilitation of Gelati urged critics not to try to damage the reputation of the ongoing work and to act according to professional ethics.

“We call on those pursuing certain subjective goals and agendas to refrain from attempts to discredit the conservation work carried out under the Gelati rehabilitation programme and deliberately mislead the public. We also call on them to return to the standards of common decency and professional ethics,” the committee said.

The committee concluded by stressing again that the work at the Gelati Monastery complex is unprecedented in scale, involves international experts and meets international conservation standards.

What happened at Gelati?

The main problem at Gelati Monastery is water and dampness, which have damaged the church’s wall paintings and mosaics over time. The situation became particularly serious after restoration work in recent years, including problems with the roof.

The problem became so serious that the UNESCO World Heritage Centre and its advisory bodies issued specific recommendations to Georgia. The authorities changed their approach to the restoration work in response to those recommendations and established the current Rehabilitation Committee.

A ruling by Georgia’s Supreme Court also notes that workers carried out roofing work at Gelati without an adequate expert assessment. The court found that problems with the materials used and the quality of the installation created a real risk of water entering the building.

Restoration of Georgia’s Gelati Monastery

World.title: Suicides in Armenia’s military: the statistics and debate over who should be held responsible
World.content:
Suicides in Armenia’s army: statistics

In Armenia, debate continues over the causes of military deaths in peacetime and who should bear responsibility. A series of suicides has prompted the latest discussions. The first incident occurred on 21 July. Then, on 13 August, the Defence Ministry reported that it had found the body of serviceman Grigor Zakaryan with a gunshot wound. In both cases, the Investigative Committee said it had opened criminal proceedings under the article on negligent incitement to suicide.

According to the Vanadzor office of the Helsinki Citizens’ Assembly, this was the 31st military death in Armenia in 2026. However, the Defence Ministry says 11 servicemen have died. Moreover, the ministry’s spokesperson said the number of military deaths had become the subject of various forms of manipulation.

“We often see reports in the press about 30 deaths in the army over the course of a year. But no one says how many of those 30 cases actually occurred in the army, which were related to military service and which were not. Even if the deaths were related to service, were all of them murders and suicides?” Aram Torosyan said, calling for greater precision.

Government bodies and civil society organisations also differ over who should bear responsibility for military deaths. Human rights groups tend to argue that the defence minister and the chief of the General Staff should be held accountable. However, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan does not share this view.

“In my assessment, it is not the case that the chief of the General Staff and the defence minister are failing to make sufficient efforts to address this issue,” Nikol Pashinyan said.

Civil society data differs from official figures

Human rights activist Nazeli Movsesyan, who represents the Vanadzor office of the Helsinki Citizens’ Assembly, said she had seen no positive changes. According to her, the number of military deaths in non-combat situations has not decreased:

“The situation is even worse than in 2025. There were 35 deaths throughout 2025, while there have already been 31 cases in the first eight months of this year.”

She stressed that 10 cases in 2025 were classified as related to military service, while the same number have been recorded in just eight months this year.

Defence Ministry spokesman Aram Torosyan says these claims do not match the official statistics.

“We have recorded 11 deaths this year. Only five of those who died were serving their mandatory military service. Some died from illness, while others died in a mine explosion,” he said.

Torosyan said six of the 11 deaths involved suicide or incitement to suicide, but only three were related to military service.

Commenting on last year’s figures, he stressed that there were no cases of murder in the army in 2025.

Causes of suicides in the army

The authorities have not released details about the death of serviceman Grigor Zakaryan. However, the prime minister said that 85-90% of suicides in the army result from:

gambling addiction and the debts it causes;

personal and family problems;

servicemen falling asleep while on duty, which can lead to conflicts with fellow soldiers.

“If a serviceman on duty at a border post falls asleep, he puts other people’s lives at risk. Soldiers then begin to treat the person who fell asleep at the post negatively, and he becomes isolated. After returning from combat duty, psychological pressure can also follow. We should not place all the blame on the army leadership. I am responsible for the fact that we have still not found a solution to this problem,” Pashinyan said.

Human rights activist Nazeli Movsesyan believes that the first two causes mentioned by the prime minister have nothing to do with the army. At the same time, she believes authorities can eliminate the third factor by taking systemic measures:

“Why does a serviceman fall asleep while on duty? Are there enough personnel to ensure that everyone gets enough rest and does not feel the need to sleep while on duty?”

Prime minister’s statements and dismissals

On the day the soldier died, Nikol Pashinyan told reporters that the government had discussed the situation and decided to make dismissals. He announced personnel changes in the Military Police and the Defence Ministry’s Department of Moral and Psychological Support:

“We will analyse in detail why our efforts in this area are not producing the desired results and draw conclusions. Yes, there must be individual accountability.”

The same day, reports emerged that Military Police chief Ashot Zakaryan had submitted his resignation. Today, the president dismissed Zakaryan from the post he had held for six years. In another decree, Major General Aram Hovhannisyan was appointed to replace him. From 2023 to 2025, he served as deputy interior minister and police chief.

There are no specific details yet about personnel changes in the Department of Moral and Psychological Support.

In recent days, the Defence Ministry has reported consultations on organising psychological support in the armed forces. To review a report on the psychological assistance provided to the military, the defence minister met professors from Yerevan State University’s Research Centre for Psychology. The ministry is also holding discussions with conscript sergeants and officers serving on duty at military posts.

“The agenda includes issues related to preventing hazing and eliminating inappropriate behaviour in the army,” the ministry said.

Comment

Human rights activist Zhanna Aleksanyan believes:

“The army’s top command, led by Suren Papikyan, must give the public a detailed explanation of the series of deaths.

Has anyone from the army’s top command visited the military unit to establish the circumstances of the soldier’s death and find out what was happening there? I strongly doubt it.

Papikyan did not even visit the military unit in the village of Azat when 15 servicemen died.

On 19 January 2023, a fire broke out in the engineering and sapper company’s premises in the village of Azat, killing 15 servicemen. Three others suffered burns of varying severity.

Then, as now, Nikol Pashinyan spoke on Papikyan’s behalf. He named those responsible and accountable. But he did not explain what the Military Police had to do with the death.

If Pashinyan knows more about the situation in the army and at military units, why is Papikyan still the defence minister?”

Suicides in Armenia’s army: statistics

World.title: Azerbaijan approves State Tourism Development Program for 2026–2030
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. The State Program for the Development of Tourism in the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2026–2030 has been approved.

President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev signed the corresponding decree.

The text of the document has been published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan.

According to the decree, the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Azerbaijan must prepare and submit to the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan its proposals on the following issues:

Within six months—revision of the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan “On Tourism” based on proposals from the State Agency for Tourism of the Republic of Azerbaijan;

Within three months—revision of the mechanism for issuing investment incentive certificates for projects related to tourism, taking into account the specific nature of tourism activities;

The conditions for providing subsidies from the state budget, as provided for in paragraph 8.8.1.3 and subparagraph 8.8.2 of the State Program;

Ensure coordination of the measures provided for in the State Program and oversight of their implementation;

Once a year, submit to the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan a report on the implementation of the measures provided for in the State Program.

- to resolve other issues arising from this decree.

According to the document, the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport of the Republic of Azerbaijan must, within three months, prepare proposals on increasing the contribution of air transport to the development of tourism and submit them to the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the same time, the State Agency for Tourism of the Republic of Azerbaijan must take the necessary measures to resolve issues arising from this decree.

The Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Azerbaijan, in conjunction with the State Agency for Tourism of the Republic of Azerbaijan, must take appropriate measures to ensure the allocation of the necessary financial resources during the annual preparation of the state budget and state investment programs of the Republic of Azerbaijan to finance the activities provided for in the State Program.

The Center for Economic Reform Analysis and Communications must monitor and evaluate the implementation of the measures outlined in the State Program, as directed by the State Agency for Tourism of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

World.title: Uzbekistan's Jizzakh, Iran's Arak forge new trade and investment ties
World.content:
Photo: the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Uzbekistan’s Jizzakh regional Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Iran’s Arak Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture have signed a memorandum of cooperation to expand trade, investment and business ties between the two regions.

This was reflected in the statement by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Uzbekistan.

The memorandum was signed in Jizzakh as part of efforts to strengthen direct contacts between businesses and create new opportunities for joint projects.

The agreement provides for expanding trade, economic and investment cooperation, establishing new business relationships and promoting joint initiatives between entrepreneurs from Jizzakh and Arak.

“The memorandum will create additional opportunities for direct business contacts, joint investment projects and the expansion of trade and economic cooperation between entrepreneurs from Jizzakh and Arak,” the Uzbekistan Chamber of Commerce and Industry said.

Under the agreement, the sides will organize mutual visits by business delegations and entrepreneurs to facilitate direct contacts and identify potential areas for cooperation.

The chambers also agreed to promote joint investment projects and encourage businesses from both regions to participate in international and specialized exhibitions, conferences and other business events held in Uzbekistan and Iran.

The agreement could provide a framework for companies to exchange information on investment opportunities, establish commercial partnerships and develop joint projects across sectors of mutual interest.

Strengthening cooperation between regional business organizations is also expected to help expand economic ties beyond national-level agreements by connecting companies directly and facilitating business-to-business interaction.

The memorandum comes as Uzbekistan and Iran seek to deepen trade and investment relations and increase the involvement of private-sector businesses in bilateral economic cooperation.

The new agreement between Jizzakh and Arak could also help identify additional opportunities for investment and trade while supporting the exchange of business experience and establishing longer-term commercial partnerships.

The sides are expected to continue cooperation through business delegation exchanges and joint participation in trade and investment events.

World.title: Azerbaijan approves regulations and structure of Agency for Small and Medium Business Dev't, Investment and Export Promotion
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. The regulations and organizational structure of the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses, Investment Promotion, and Export in the Republic of Azerbaijan, under the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Azerbaijan, have been approved.

President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev signed the corresponding decree.

The text of the document has been published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan.

According to the decree, central executive authorities, public legal entities established by the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan or the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Azerbaijan and authorized under their charters to participate in the preparation of draft normative legal acts, as well as legal entities owned by the state and those in which the controlling stake (shares) is owned by the state, shall ensure that draft normative legal acts prepared by them that may affect micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, investment and export activities are coordinated with the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-sized Businesses, Investment and Export Promotion under the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Azerbaijan before being submitted to the rule-making body, in accordance with Article 46 of the Constitutional Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan “On Normative Legal Acts.”

Central executive authorities must also ensure that the regulatory legal acts they draft in these areas are adopted in consultation with the Agency.

This decree comes into effect on October 1, 2026.

World.title: Azerbaijan to commemorate Aziz Aliyev’s 130th birth anniversary
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. The 130th anniversary of the birth of Aziz Aliyev, an outstanding Azerbaijani statesman and scholar, will be commemorated.

President Ilham Aliyev signed the corresponding decree.

The text of the document has been published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan.

The decree notes that January 2027 marks the 130th anniversary of the birth of Aziz Aliyev, an outstanding Azerbaijani statesman and scientist, healthcare administrator, Doctor of Medical Sciences, and professor.

“As a true intellectual patriot, devoted to lofty ideals and humanistic values, Aziz Aliyev led a life of distinction and is one of those rare individuals who have left future generations a vivid example of service to the people. While serving in various senior positions, guided by a sense of national responsibility, he consistently carried out highly effective work in state-building and the improvement of the governance system.

Aziz Aliyev played an exceptional role in reshaping Azerbaijan’s healthcare system on a new foundation, developing medical education in accordance with the standards of his time, and training qualified national professionals in this field. During World War II, he successfully led a number of important initiatives of significant military and political importance.

At pivotal moments in Azerbaijan’s history, his decisive actions regarding issues of vital importance to the people enriched the tradition of public administration. “Aziz Aliyev’s selflessness and his contribution to further strengthening relations between Azerbaijan and Dagestan have made his name a true symbol of friendship and brotherhood between our peoples,” the Decree reads.

According to the decree, the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan, in conjunction with the Ministry of Science and Education of the Republic of Azerbaijan and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan, must prepare and implement a plan of events commemorating the 130th anniversary of the birth of the distinguished statesman and scientist Aziz Aliyev.

The Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Azerbaijan must resolve any issues arising from this decree.

World.title: Uzbekistan commissions 20-MW Chorbog wind power plant
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Uzbekistan has commissioned the 20-megawatt “Chorbog” wind farm in the Bostanliq District of the Tashkent Region, thereby increasing its renewable energy capacity.

This was announced in a statement published by Uzbekhydroenergo.

According to the information, the commissioning ceremony was held on August 20 and attended by China’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan Yu Jun, representatives of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, energy and construction companies, Uzbekhydroenergo officials, and representatives of the Tashkent regional and Bostanliq district administrations.

The project was developed as part of expanding cooperation between Uzbekistan and China. The Chinese government provided a $28 million grant to finance its implementation.

Uzbekhydroenergo carried out the organizational, technical, and engineering work for the project, including construction and installation, connection to the electricity grid, preparation of supporting infrastructure, and installation of modern wind turbines.

The plant is equipped with four wind turbines, each with a capacity of 5 MW, giving the facility a total capacity of 20 MW.

The Chorbog plant is expected to generate up to 50 million kilowatt-hours of clean electricity annually, enough to meet the electricity needs of approximately 20,000 households.

“The commissioning of the Chorbog wind power plant marks another important step in expanding renewable energy generation and strengthening Uzbekistan’s energy security,” Uzbekhydroenergo said.

The additional generation capacity is also expected to reduce pressure on the electricity grid and contribute to greater stability of Uzbekistan’s energy system.

The plant will also help reduce the use of fossil fuels by saving natural gas and coal annually and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.

The project is part of Uzbekistan’s broader efforts to diversify its energy sector, expand renewable energy generation and support the transition toward a greener economy.

The commissioning of the plant also coincides with preparations for Uzbekistan’s 35th anniversary of independence, with officials describing the facility as a contribution to the country’s renewable energy development.

The opening ceremony also featured an exhibition and awards ceremony for young artists who participated in the “Wind Power Plant Through the Eyes of Young Artists” competition organized as part of the event.

World.title: Azerbaijani journalists explore Silk Road Samarkand tourist center (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. A delegation of Azerbaijani media representatives currently visiting Uzbekistan toured the Silk Road Samarkand international tourist center, one of the country’s largest tourism projects.

Twenty representatives from Azerbaijan’s leading media outlets are participating in the press tour. Among the participants is Emin Aliyev, editor-in-chief of the Trend International News Agency.

The complex is located along the Samarkand Irrigation Canal and covers approximately 260 hectares. Eight hotels have been built here, capable of accommodating more than 3,000 guests at a time, along with 14 villas, restaurants, parks, recreational areas, and an international convention center. The 2.2-kilometer-long rowing canal is one of the complex’s central features.

The “Eternal City” historical and ethnographic park holds a special place within Silk Road Samarkand. Covering an area of about 11 hectares, it recreates the atmosphere of an ancient Eastern city with narrow streets, squares, artisan workshops, cafes, galleries, and venues for cultural events. The project concept was developed with the participation of renowned Uzbek artist Bobur Ismoilov. The architectural designs blend motifs from Parthian, Hellenistic, and Islamic cultures.

“The Eternal City” showcases traditional crafts from various regions of Uzbekistan, including ceramics, woodcarving, carpet weaving, jewelry making, and the production of the famous Samarkand paper made from mulberry bark.

The press tour participants visited Firdavs Umarov’s workshop, where the tradition of making Samarkand silk paper is being revived. According to the master craftsman, he has devoted 25 years to reviving this craft. The paper is made from mulberry bark without any chemical additives: the raw material is boiled, ground, shaped into sheets, and pressed, after which each sheet is polished with a stone. The entire process takes several days.

“Samarkand paper has been known since the Middle Ages and became widespread in Central Asia. Thanks to its durability and smooth surface, it was used for manuscripts, calligraphy, and miniatures,” the master said.

Journalists also got acquainted with the secrets of making Samarkand ceramics. One of the masters, Sharif Azimov, a ceramic artist and potter from the Uzbekistan Academy of Arts, explained that he has been practicing this craft for 56 years. Speaking about his creative journey, Sharif Azimov noted that his interest in the craft began back in his school years. He began working with ceramics under the guidance of the renowned Samarkand master Umarkul Jurakulov.

“I was in eighth or ninth grade at the time. We would visit Umarkul Jurakulov’s workshop, and ever since then I’ve loved this art form, which has been my life’s work for 56 years now,” the master said.

According to him, it was the Jurakulov School that laid the foundation for his professional career.

Today, the master not only continues the traditions of the Samarkand ceramics school but also passes on his knowledge to the younger generation. According to Azimov, his students come from various countries.

“I have many students from Azerbaijan. There are also students from the Caribbean. They are continuing my research,” he noted.

Azimov emphasized that, for him, ceramics is not simply about producing objects, but about continuing Samarkand’s centuries-old artistic tradition.

His own creative method is linked to the study of the history of ceramics and ancient examples. Researchers note that the master carefully studied museum exhibits and historical techniques, and in his work, he developed the traditions of the Samarkand school of ceramics.

Silk Road Samarkand officially opened on August 23, 2022. The project combines hospitality, cultural, medical, business, and recreational infrastructure and is focused, in particular, on the development of international, business, and event tourism.

The complex’s name reflects Samarkand’s historical significance as one of the key hubs of trade and cultural exchange along the Great Silk Road. Today, Silk Road Samarkand strives to combine this historical legacy with modern tourism infrastructure, creating a new international image for the ancient city.

World.title: Kazakh Solidcore Resources, Oman's MDO sign MoU on mining cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Kazakhstan-based gold producer Solidcore Resources plc and Minerals Development Oman (MDO) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) establishing a framework for cooperation and knowledge exchange in the mining sector, the company said.

“The non-binding MoU outlines potential forms of cooperation, including short-term personnel secondments, technical placements at operational sites, workshops and training, exchange of best practices, and joint technical working groups”, Solidcore Resources said.

The parties identified several potential areas of cooperation, including geology and exploration, mining, mineral processing and metallurgy, production and operational practices, technical and project development, health and safety, environment and sustainability.

Solidcore and MDO intend to subsequently negotiate a definitive Agreement on Knowledge Transfer and Technical Cooperation, which will supersede the MoU and establish detailed terms for future cooperation.

The agreement follows a visit by an Omani delegation led by Abdulsalam Al Murshidi, President of the Oman Investment Authority and Chairman of the Board of Directors of Solidcore Resources, to Kazakhstan. The delegation met with Solidcore's management and visited the company's Kyzyl mine and processing plant.

Maaden International Investment, a fund wholly owned by the Government of Oman, is Solidcore's largest shareholder, holding a 31.7% stake.

Solidcore Resources is a gold producer registered in Kazakhstan's Astana International Financial Centre and listed on the Astana International Exchange. The company's gold equivalent production increased 56% year-on-year to 86,000 ounces in the second quarter of 2026 and 71% to 210,000 ounces in the first half of 2026, driven by third-party concentrate processing.

MDO is a state-owned mining investment and development company in the Sultanate of Oman.

World.title: North Korea fires missiles into sea as South Korea, US hold military drills
World.content:
North Korea has fired several short-range ballistic missiles into the sea, according to South Korea's military, a day after Seoul announced it was scaling back its military drills with the United States.

The Joint Chiefs of Staff said about 10 short-range ballistic missiles were launched from Pyongyang towards North Korea's eastern waters at around 5pm local time on Thursday.

South Korea's presidential national security council held an emergency meeting following the missile launches and issued a statement urging North Korea to halt ballistic missile launches that are banned by UN Security Council resolutions.

South Korea has since bolstered its surveillance posture and said it was closely coordinating information with the United States and Japan.

The Japanese prime minister's office also confirmed it had detected a suspected missile launch.

South Korea has reduced its training drills with the United States from 11 days to five. (AP: Ahn Young-joon)

The missile launch comes amid the US and South Korea's annual military training drills and less than a day after US President Donald Trump said he planned to meet North Korea leader Kim Jong Un later this year.

Trump says he will meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un later this year The US president made the announcement days after ordering the US scale back its military drills with South Korea.

The training drills will end six days early this year after Mr Trump ordered the Pentagon to scale back the exercise.

The Ulchi Freedom Shield is one of the main military exercises conducted by the US and South Korea each year to enhance their ability to cope with potential North Korean aggression.

While Washington and Seoul say their drills are defensive in nature, North Korea calls them an invasion rehearsal and often reacts with weapons tests.

Before this month's drills started, North Korea accused the US and South Korea of plotting more provocative exercises this summer and vowed to respond with "a new level of a deterrent".

China weighs in on Korean Peninsula tensions

South Korean National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac meets with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Seoul. (Yonhap via Reuters)

Thursday's missile launch also came as China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited South Korea.

During the visit, the foreign minister urged South Korea not to take sides between Beijing and Washington, saying the US should abandon its "hostile" policy towards North Korea to ease tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

"The fundamental solution to the tensions on the Korean Peninsula lies in addressing the root causes of the problem and urging the United States to abandon its hostile policy toward North Korea," he said, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua, during a meeting with South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac.

China hopes South Korea will "achieve genuine strategic autonomy, refrain from bloc confrontation and taking sides, and develop relations with major powers including China and the United States in parallel and without contradiction".

North Korea also fired a short-range ballistic missile over the Sea of Japan earlier this month, a day after Pyongyang criticised Japan's military build-up in the region.

AP/Reuters

World.title: Russian missile strikes kill 13 in Kyiv, more than 30 injured
World.content:
Russian ballistic missiles have killed at least 13 people and injured more than 30 in Kyiv, authorities say, damaging buildings and severing power supply to some parts of the Ukrainian capital.

A fire broke out, and the upper floors of a nine-storey residential block were destroyed in the city's Solomianskyi district, where seven people were killed, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, calling for Friday to be observed as a day of mourning.

Two other districts also suffered damage, Mr Klitschko said on the Telegram messaging app, with non-residential facilities, warehouses, a school and a children's hospital hit.

Power company DTEK said it restored electricity to more than half of the roughly 90,000 homes left without power in the capital following the attack.

Russia has intensified its air strikes on Ukraine over the summer. (Reuters: Anatolii Stepanov)

"There used to be a building here, and now it's gone," said 45-year-old resident Maria Abramova.

She had only just reached her children's room after the air raid alert sounded when explosions rang out, blowing her windows out and "nearly killing" her husband.

Russia has stepped up air strikes on Ukraine in recent months, trying to exploit its smaller neighbour's critical shortage of interceptors to down ballistic missiles.

The Russian defence ministry said Moscow attacked Kyiv and the surrounding region with air strikes and drones, hitting facilities producing drone components, a military depot and a logistics hub, as well as other targets.

A woman in Kyiv reacts after finding out her grandson has died in the Russian attacks. (Reuters: Anatolii Stepanov)

A resident reported hearing more than a dozen explosions. In the region around the Ukrainian capital, another person was killed, an official said on Telegram.

Ukraine's emergency service showed video of servicemen battling a blaze in a building and helping people to escape facilities destroyed during the night in Kyiv.

Ukraine has also increased its attacks on Russia, targeting oil facilities and logistics infrastructure to try to undermine Moscow's ability to wage war.

Smoke rises from a food warehouse hit by a Russian missile strike near Kyiv. (Reuters: Valentyn Ogirenko)

Diplomatic efforts have failed so far to yield a lasting ceasefire in the war, which started with Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Russian bank fires economist Andrei Klepach, one of Russia's most prominent macroeconomists, has predicted a social crisis and says costs are "mounting" over the Ukraine war.

A drone crashed into NATO and European Union member Romania during the Russian attack on Ukraine, the Romanian defence ministry said on Thursday. A drone also crossed Moldova's airspace, the country's military said.

Ukraine had handed proposals to US negotiators, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, for a plan to end the war, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said this month, and he has also repeatedly asked for interceptor missiles to ward off missile attacks.

Russia did not receive specific proposals for possible new meetings with US negotiators, foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told the Izvestia newspaper.

But she added that Moscow would be ready to arrange a meeting at short notice.

Mr Witkoff and Mr Kushner were last in Moscow last January and have not yet visited Kyiv.

Wires/ABC

World.title: 'Is this accurate?' How one note magnified the tragedy of bushwalker's family
World.content:
"Is this accurate?"

That was the immediate reaction of New South Wales Premier Chris Minns when he was passed a note in parliament shortly before midday.

He had already faced two hours of questioning in a budget estimates hearing and still had another hour to go.

The note was a surprising, but welcome distraction from questions about uranium mining.

After being assured the information was credible, the premier made an announcement that brought joy to the room.

"We've got some fantastic news, Mr Chair," he said.

"Lily Hooper has been found alive."

The NSW premier was handed the note during budget estimates. (ABC News)

There were murmurs of relief from MPs, many of whom had been following the news about the missing 18-year-old hiker.

Ms Hooper left her home south-west of Sydney on the morning of Wednesday, August 12, to go hiking in the Nattai National Park.

Her car was later found near the Bonnum Pic Walking Trail, sparking a large-scale multi-agency search involving nearly 1,000 people, according to police.

The premier went on to thank the police, the State Emergency Service (SES), defence personnel and the many others who had joined the search.

It was a moment of levity in a sometimes combative hearing.

The premier's announcement was widely reported, including by the ABC.

About 25 minutes later, the premier was handed another note, containing the worst possible news.

A tragic miscommunication

Lily Hooper's body was found after an eight-day search. (Supplied: NSW Police)

By that stage, the hearing had resumed normal programming, with opposition MP Natalie Ward asking a series of pointed questions about the office of local government.

After conferring with Secretary of the Cabinet Office, Kate Boyd, a stony-faced Mr Minns made another announcement.

"I've got some terrible news," he said.

"I apologise to the committee, but it seems as if the early advice was wrong.

"Lily's body's been found, and she's been found deceased."

"Oh my god," replied committee chair Jeremy Buckingham.

Members of the Australia Defence Force also joined the search. (ABC News: Billy Cooper)

The premier continued.

"I only raise that because I made the earlier advice and I'm very sorry for that," he said.

"This is obviously devastating, and I'm just profoundly sad for her family and all those concerned."

Police said about 11:30am a body believed to be that of Ms Hooper was located in bushland.

The premier's anguish was plain to see.

Not only had he been provided with incorrect information, but his earlier statement had brought the community an immense sense of relief that was abruptly snatched away.

People would be entitled to wonder how such an error could be made.

It soon became clear the miscommunication occurred much further down the chain.

Unfortunately, it made its way to the top before anyone could stop it.

The error fuelled by 'elation'

The NSW assistant police commissioner said there was a delay in effectively communicating the fact that Lily Hooper had died. (ABC News: Brooke Chandler)

Speaking to reporters in the Southern Highlands, NSW Police Assistant Commissioner Joseph Cassar pointed to the communication challenges search teams were facing using handheld radios.

An SES volunteer made the initial discovery and was following protocol by reporting it up, he said.

However, he said there was a delay in effectively communicating the fact that Ms Hooper had died.

During the intervening period of between eight and 10 minutes, Ms Hooper's family, who were in close contact with the police, were led to believe she was alive.

Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon apologised "unreservedly" to the family.

"The miscommunication obviously was born out of elation that Lily had been found, and her condition at that time was such that searchers were relieved," he said.

"Certainly, those at the command post were elated.

"Tragically, that miscommunication then led to a deflation, and obviously we know now the impact on her family."

By that stage, the initial report of Ms Hooper having been found had already found its way to the government.

Police have well-established lines of communication into the offices of both the premier and the police minister, Yasmin Catley.

Word travels fast, by necessity.

During media conferences or Question Time, both are regularly asked for updates on police investigations or emergency operations, so they need to be well-briefed.

A large-scale multi-agency search was launched. (ABC News: Billy Cooper)

Just as the public is right to expect that the information the premier provides is accurate, he is right to expect the information being passed up the chain is correct.

The commissioner said the incorrect report was passed via police commands into the offices of both the premier and the police minister.

While he "wasn't given notice" of the premier's announcement, he was not surprised that he had made it.

"When Lily was located, obviously there was elation," Commissioner Lanyon said.

"That information got passed through very quickly.

"It's unsurprising that it went quickly up into government."

Police have now committed to reviewing and improving their communication on the ground, particularly when working with the SES.

It is also likely to prompt some rebalancing between the speed and accuracy of the information they provide to the government, which today showed how quickly it can disseminate it.

On this occasion, that balance was off, magnifying both a mistake and a family's tragedy.

World.title: 'Completely unacceptable': Albanese lashes AFL over response to Swans scandal
World.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has criticised the AFL over its handling of the current scandal engulfing the league.

On Wednesday, the Swans stood down five players for the rest of the AFL season — vice captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey — for breaching club standards for drinking and bringing women to the hotel.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad have since flown to New South Wales and are investigating a report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a player allegedly touching one of the women without her consent.

Swans players James Jordon, Chad Warner, Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey and Riley Bice have been stood down. (Getty Images/ABC News)

Mr Albanese told 7.30 that he felt the initial response was not good enough.

"It's extraordinary that this has occurred," Mr Albanese said.

"The idea that this is occurring is completely untenable, and the initial response as well was, I think, completely unacceptable.

"The NRL have a no-fault stand down clause for issues like this, but the first thoughts should have been always about women and their safety.

" I don't think that occurred at this time. The AFL certainly needs to do better. "

That initial response came on Monday afternoon when Swans CEO and Fremantle Dockers great Matthew Pavlich confirmed several players had been linked to the alleged incident.

Sydney Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich has issued several statements this week. (Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe)

"We’re still piecing together exactly what’s transpired here and have our own set of internal inquiries ongoing," Mr Pavlich said on Monday.

"But safe to say that we’re extremely shocked and disappointed that this has taken place and that the players have found themselves in this situation."

On Tuesday AFL CEO Andrew Dillon described the allegations as "deeply disturbing" in a statement.

On Thursday night the ABC reported that detectives investigating have been told some players paid female adult entertainers to consume drugs off their bodies.

Police have not made any arrests or laid charges.

Mr Albanese said the AFL and the Swans should "have a good look" at their culture.

Albanese to press Israel over Frankcom

While Mr Albanese was focused on several issues at home, the major geopolitical issue of the day involved Israel.

On Wednesday night, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) cleared its personnel of any criminal wrongdoing over a 2024 strike on a humanitarian convoy, which killed Australian woman Zomi Frankcom.

Ms Frankcom was killed in a strike by the IDF. (Supplied: Facebook)

The decision was described as an "outrage" by Foreign Minister Penny Wong on Thursday morning.

Mr Albanese told 7.30 he wanted a much more transparent response from the Israeli government.

"It clearly is an outrage and there's a need for a far more transparent and clear explanation from the Israeli government other than what we've received," Mr Albanese said.

Asked if that would involve an independent investigation, Mr Albanese said it was one option.

"It's certainly not good enough that on World Humanitarian Day ... they release this so-called report that essentially says, 'Yes, we're responsible, but nothing to see here', he said".

"Zomi represented the best of Australians out there in a dangerous area, helping her fellow global citizens as she had in other parts of the world that were suffering conflict as well. And that's why it deserves better.

"Her family deserved better, and frankly, Australia deserves better.

"We will press the Israeli government.

"[We] will discuss with Ms Frankcom's family. They deserve to be consulted on these issues and we'll do that, and then we'll make an announcement in coming days."

PM concedes podcast appearance was 'an error'

The Prime Minister was also asked about criticism he's faced over several comments he made on the Deep Bush podcast.

Loading...

Mr Albanese first came under scrutiny for playing "shag, marry, date" on the podcast, which was broadcast in July.

He has since unequivocally apologised for saying he would "shag" Kylie Minogue.

Recently it was hand gestures he made on the podcast, while referring to a pair of melons given to him by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, that caused controversy.

Mr Albanese has not apologised specifically for the melon interaction and maintains that the gestures have been misinterpreted.

Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. (Reuters: Hollie Adams)

However, he told 7.30 that in hindsight he should not have gone on the podcast and that he had learned from it.

"I learned that I need to do better every day," Mr Albanese said.

"If I had my time again ... then I wouldn't have done that podcast.

" We have a view which is trying to talk to as many people as possible, but clearly that was an error. "

Watch 7.30, Mondays to Thursdays 7:30pm on ABC iview and ABC TV

World.title: Zomi Frankcom's family 'deeply disappointed' IDF won't pursue charges
World.content:
The family of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, who was killed in an Israeli strike while delivering humanitarian aid in Gaza in 2024, has slammed the Israeli military's decision not to pursue criminal charges against the commanders who ordered the attack.

The statement, issued by Zomi's brother Mal on behalf of the Frankcom family, said family members were "deeply disappointed" by the decision, having spent the past two years waiting for justice while "hoping and calling for an independent criminal investigation".

"Zomi and her colleagues deserve more than an internal, opaque process that ends with a short statement by the Israeli military absolving their soldiers of criminal wrongdoing," they said.

" The families of the victims deserve transparency and an independent judicial assessment of the criminal responsibility for the international humanitarian law violations that took place on that day. "

Ms Frankcom was one of seven World Central Kitchen aid workers killed on April 1, 2024, while taking part in a convoy helping to deliver food and other supplies to northern Gaza.

The group was travelling in three armoured cars branded with the World Central Kitchen logo, and driving through part of the Gaza Strip that had been declared a "humanitarian fire control zone" while coordinating movements with the IDF (Israel Defense Forces).

An Israeli drone fired three missiles at the convoy — one at each of the cars in succession — as survivors of the initial strike attempted to move from one vehicle to another.

Wreckage of one of three World Central Kitchen vehicles destroyed in the strikes. (Reuters: Ahmed Zakot)

An Australian investigation into the Israeli government's response to the incident, led by retired defence chief Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, found the deaths had been the result of the first vehicle being misidentified due to a number of factors, including the presence of armed security in the vicinity, confirmation bias and a "failure within the IDF to fully disseminate and/or read the detailed movement plan approved by the convoy".

Wong declares 'difficult time' in relations with Israel Foreign Minister Penny Wong says she has "no confidence" in the IDF investigation that cleared Israeli soldiers of criminal wrongdoing.

The subsequent strikes were also found to be a breach of IDF procedures and the rules of engagement, echoing the findings of a rapid FFAM ("fact-finding and assessment mechanism") investigation conducted by the IDF in the days following the incident.

Two IDF officers were fired in the weeks after the strikes, while others were reprimanded.

In their statement released on Thursday evening, Ms Frankcom's family expressed disagreement with the finding that there was no wrongdoing involved that merited at least a criminal investigation, highlighting the follow-up strikes as well as the fact that one of the officers involved had reportedly signed a letter earlier that year calling for the flow of aid to Gaza to be restricted.

They also expressed outrage at the timing of the announcement, which came on World Humanitarian Day, an internationally recognised day dedicated to those who have died working for humanitarian causes.

A humanitarian award has since been created in Ms Frankcom's name. (Supplied: X)

The family had been standing alongside Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong at an event at Parliament House just hours prior to the announcement, launching a humanitarian award in Ms Frankcom's name.

"For it to be announced on World Humanitarian Day, the day the world pauses to remember those who have lost their lives while helping others … is an insult to my sister's memory," Ms Frankcom's brother Mal said.

Senator Wong similarly expressed anger at the announcement, saying she had no confidence in the IDF's findings, and calling in Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, to explain the decision.

Calling today's events a "difficult time" in diplomatic relations with Israel, she said she was informed of the IDF's decision just minutes before it was publicly announced, and did not have time to alert Ms Frankcom's family.

World.title: Proposed gun reforms 'betrayal of Tasmanians', critics say
World.content:
The Tasmanian government's watered-down gun law reforms have been described as "extraordinarily weak" and a "betrayal of Tasmanians" by Labor and the Greens.

The proposed reforms, which were tabled in state parliament on Thursday, were a response to calls to tighten gun laws in the wake of last year's Bondi terror attack.

But gun control advocates say the legislation tabled today is even "weaker" than the much-criticised draft legislation released earlier this year.

The bill still does not include a limit on the number of guns one person can own, despite the state's Police Commissioner Donna Adams calling for it.

It still reclassifies straight pull and button or lever release shotguns to the more restrictive Category C and introduces an Australian citizenship requirement for owners, with carve-outs for New Zealand citizens and people who need them for work.

But it now grandfathers these clauses, meaning the rules do not apply to guns that people already own or to non-citizens who currently own legal guns.

One gun advocate says "law-abiding firearms owners probably aren't going to be too happy" with the reforms. (ABC News)

Greens' police spokesperson Tabatha Badger said the bill was "deeply disappointing" and "simply not good enough".

"Tasmanians expected so much more when it came to firearm safety in this state," she said.

"We'd already seen a draft bill out for public consultation that was underwhelming, and what we've seen today tabled in this parliament is an incredible disappointment.

"It's very clear that this police minister does not understand that public safety is a core part of his job."

Tabatha Badger says the government should be "incredibly ashamed" of its proposal. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Ms Badger cited the Port Arthur shootings of 1996 and raised concerns about the grandfathering of clauses, the decision to include changes to antique gun laws and the addition of mandatory minimum sentences for stolen firearms.

"This Liberal government should be incredibly ashamed of what they have put forward," she said.

"Tasmania was a state that, in the past, has led the way off the back of incredible tragedy to reform firearms to help make our community safer. In the years that have followed, we simply haven't kept up with that."

What we know about guns in Australia Gun control researchers say we have "no idea" how many black market and 3D-printed weapons are out there.

Labor leader Josh Willie accused the government of being "soft on crime".

"This is a betrayal of Tasmanians and community safety by Premier Rockliff," he said.

"He has a position to support unlimited guns.

" He's backflipped on his position to improve community safety and I think, rightly, Tasmanians will be questioning whether he's got their back. "

Bill defended by police minister

The bill also follows through on a 2024 election promise of no licence requirements for antique firearms.

Antique firearms manufactured before January 1, 1900 will only have to be registered with Tasmania Police.

Police Minister Felix Ellis said the legislation strikes the right balance and will result in a significant uplift in community safety.

Police Minister Felix Ellis has defended the changes, saying Tasmanians will be safer as a result of the reforms. (Facebook: Felix Ellis)

He defended the grandfathered clauses, saying they were about "ensuring that the transition is right".

"That we can continue to support people who are farmers, hunters and recreational shooters who have been complying with the law," he said.

"We had people who have lived here for decades, who are not citizens of Australia, but have complied with our laws here in Tasmania when it comes to their firearms and [are of] good character, so rather than unduly penalising those people, it allows us to establish a framework moving forward."

Mr Ellis also said the mandatory minimum sentences for stolen firearms were particularly important.

"It'll ensure that if you steal a firearm or you're caught in possession of a stolen firearm you will go to jail," he said.

"That is absolutely vital so we can ensure that illegal firearms are not being used to intimidate our community and aren't being used to fuel organised crime."

An agreement to reclassify guns has been grandfathered, prompting backlash. (ABC News)

The bill will support the implementation of the National Firearms Register in the state, which the minister said would improve intelligence sharing between law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

"We've seen that the failures of Bondi have been very much about the failure to share intelligence, particularly about people who are seeking to do harm in the community," Mr Ellis said.

"So this uplift will be critical."

Opposition to push amendments

Gun Control Australia vice president Roland Browne accused the Tasmanian government of going sideways and backwards.

"The agreement reached in December required reclassification of guns and Tasmania has done that, but then they've grandfathered the clauses that make those reclassification decisions operative.

"In other words, if people are going to have their guns reclassified … shooters in Tasmania keep their guns.

" How is that going to make Tasmania a safer place? "

Roland Browne questions the efficacy of the proposed reforms. (ABC News: Monty Jacka)

But nor were gun advocates satisfied.

In a social media video, Tasmanian Shooters Union President Phillip Bigg said it didn't seem like their consultations were taken note of.

"Law-abiding firearms owners probably aren't going to be too happy," he said.

"I've had a quick look, doesn't look very good."

Mr Bigg also acknowledged that Labor and the Greens were likely to try to make their own amendments to the bill.

That was confirmed by both parties today, with Mr Willie telling the media the party is still intent on introducing caps on guns.

"We've said consistently we'll promote community safety while respecting the legitimate ownership of legal firearms owners," he said.

"We'll work with the parliament around amendments. We're committed to doing that."

Phillip Bigg says the Tasmanian Shooters Union would work with parliament on the amendments. (ABC News)

The two parties combined will need to find another four votes to get any amendments through the lower house.

The state government said there will be a six-month voluntary buyback scheme that will begin once the bill has royal assent.

It is still in negotiations with the federal government about the cost.

Parliament is set to debate the bill in the first week of September.

World.title: ‘Clearly, that was an error’: Albanese wouldn’t do podcast if had time again
World.content:
NationalPolitical leadership ‘Clearly, that was an error’: Albanese wouldn’t do podcast if had time again Jack Gramenz August 20, 2026 — 9:40pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says it was an error to make an appearance on a podcast episode that led to weeks of criticism. “If I had my time again, which you don’t, then I wouldn’t have done that podcast,” Albanese told ABC’s 7.30 on Thursday. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese opposite Nikki Osborne on the Bush Deep podcast which aired in July. Bush Deep Podcast “We have a view which is trying to talk to as many people as possible, but clearly, that was an error,” Albanese said. The prime minister’s appearance opposite Nikki Osborne on an episode of the Bush Deep podcast, which aired in early July, spawned some uproars.



The first came over a game of “marry, date, shag” when he nominated pop star Kylie Minogue for “all of the above”. He subsequently apologised, facing heavy criticism from political opponents saying he had demonstrated a lack of judgment and should have known better than to play along with the inappropriate game. But the controversy escalated as parliament returned earlier in August, when Japan’s former ambassador to Australia Shingo Yamagami wrote in The Australian that Albanese made an “insulting” gesture while talking about crown melons gifted to him by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in May. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese accepts a Shizuoka crown melon from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in Canberra in May. x.com/takaichi_sanae During the podcast, filmed at The Lodge, Osborne joked to Albanese about Takaichi smuggling the crown melons under her shirt “like Pamela Anderson”. Albanese then gestured with both hands as he told Osborne the gift had been “a couple of melons”. Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi appeared at a press conference alongside Australian counterpart Richard Marles in Canberra this week, playing down the controversy.

World.title: Perth dad dies after allegedly being attacked by ‘group of Aussies’ in a Bali bar
World.content:
NationalWACourts Perth dad dies after allegedly being attacked by ‘group of Aussies’ in a Bali bar Rebecca Peppiatt and Amber Wilkinson August 20, 2026 — 9:31pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A Perth father has died after being allegedly attacked by a group of Australians while on holiday in Bali. Paul Dougan, from Gosnells, underwent three surgeries, including to have his spleen removed, after the attack 10 days ago. Paul Dougan has died after allegedly being set upon by a group of Aussies in a Bali bar 10 days ago. He was on a trip with friends when he was allegedly assaulted at One Tribe bar in Kuta by a group of strangers, believed to be Australian, after his friends had left to go home. “To have this happen to him, of all people, is just devastating,” friend David Coughtrie told 9News Perth.



“He’s not the kind of guy to go looking for that sort of trouble. “He’d grabbed his partner and said, ‘Let’s get out of here’. As he stood up he was confronted by a person that said, ‘What did you say?’ and pretty much didn’t wait for an answer and just struck him.” Perth father Paul Dougan has been hospitalised in Bali after allegedly being assaulted by fellow Australians while on holiday. GoFundMe Dougan’s injuries included 10 broken ribs and severe internal bleeding. His family rushed to Bali to be with him and on Wednesday his son Liam launched a GoFundMe page to help pay for mounting medical costs.



But as donations started pouring in, Dougan lost his battle while in intensive care. Related Article Inquest Behind bars for 30 years, out for 79 days: Perth inquest probes complex final months of a killer Liam posted to social media saying, “it wasn’t meant to be this way Dad”, adding, “I will love and remember you for the rest of my life and I will continue to make you proud. “I am shattered, lost, heartbroken and confused but grateful I ever got to call you my Dad,” the post, made on Thursday evening, read. Liam had earlier made a video explaining what had happened and how Indonesian police were in the process of trying to track down those responsible.



“It looks to be a group of four of the suspects that we’ve got and [they were] beating him heavily while on the floor,” he said. On the fundraising page, Liam wrote his father was “brutally assaulted by a group of Australians who are yet to be identified”. “They beat and kicked him multiple times putting him in a life-threatening condition,” it read. “From this Paul suffered internal bleeding and 10 broken ribs, has undergone three major surgeries, had his spleen removed, required four blood transfusions, and currently has drains in both his lungs and abdomen as a result of the internal injuries and bleeding from the attack. “He has now been in ICU for 10 days and remains sedated following his third surgery.”



On Thursday evening the fundraiser had received more than $45,000 in donations. With 9News Perth

World.title: Swill waters run deep
World.content:
“Apropos David Sayers’ soft drink saga (C8), in my teens, I worked at the local lolly water factory in Muswellbrook in the holidays,” writes Denis Cartledge of Tenterfield. “It was a Friday afternoon event for one particular worker to be thrown in the softwater tank that supplied the factory. He rarely washed, and his workmates thought they’d help his cleanliness regime. Looking back, I don’t think the tank was drained, cleaned and/or refilled. It was around that time we decided to stop buying a mixed crate of lolly water every few months.”

The current dress code discussion (C8) is revealing a few workarounds. Here’s Bev Matthews of Wallerawang: “Back in the early ’80s, three friends and I tried to get into a club in Parramatta. One of the boys had a collarless shirt on, and they wouldn’t let him in. I happened to be wearing a knitted cardigan with a collar (like I said, it was the ’80s). He donned it, and voilà, they let him in.”

“In the late 1970s, my brother-in-law went for an after work beer at the Manly Yacht Club in Brisbane, of which he was a member,” says Colleen Riga of Potts Point. “Clad in his work gear consisting of boots, stubbies and polo shirt, he was told that club rules required a tie for evening entry. They had no problem with the work gear, so, looking through a box under the counter containing ‘emergency neckwear’ they presented him with a clip-on bow-tie (or ‘blowfly’ as he incorrectly heard) and he was free to enjoy a coldie.”

Reading about Mash McDonald’s in Iran (C8) reminded Ann MacKenzie of St Ives of the time she was in Tehran in 2017 and noticed a fast food establishment dubbed ZFC.

In reply to Stephen Tait’s inquiry into the wellbeing of Dirranbandi pubsters the Norton Brothers (C8), Janice Creenaune of Austinmer says the visit was earlier in the year, on Anzac Day in fact, and that the pub was “heaving with 2-up patrons. However, today we are off to camp near the ‘Hog and Billy’ in Girilambone, (known colloquially as ‘Girl’ I believe). Is there anybody we can look up for you there, Stephen?”

World.title: Turnbull-backed battery proposal sets off sparks in Doreen
World.content:
PoliticsVictoriaCity life Turnbull-backed battery proposal sets off sparks in Doreen Adam Carey August 20, 2026 — 7:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A renewable energy company chaired by former prime minister Malcolm Turnbull plans to build a large-scale battery on bushfire-prone land in Melbourne’s green wedges, alarming nearby residents who lived through the devastating Black Saturday fires of 2009. The proposed lithium-ion battery energy storage system could potentially store enough electricity to power almost 90,000 homes for a day. It would be built at an estimated cost of $500 million. Locals Sarah Hunter, Alicia Hynes, Barbara Marshall, Gareth Davies and Mel Nelson stand opposite the proposed big battery site. Ruby Alexander But the project has startled the small semi-rural communities of Doreen and Arthurs Creek on Melbourne’s north-eastern fringe, where residents only learnt of the proposal when a handful of neighbours were contacted by a communications agency on Tuesday. The Middle Hut BESS project, which had been kept under wraps until this week, is at an advanced stage of planning, with its developers, Turnbull Renewables, poised to apply directly to the state government for a planning permit next month.



Turnbull Renewables said the property had been chosen because it sat beneath two high-voltage transmission lines, meaning the battery could be plugged directly into Melbourne’s energy grid. “The site sits along the existing 330kV and 220 kV high-voltage transmission lines, the backbone of Victoria’s electricity network … [It] has been strategically chosen to store and dispatch energy close to metropolitan Melbourne,” the company said. It said the site was one of few along the transmission line corridor with the environmental conditions needed to support a battery system, and had been positioned away from homes. The battery system would cover about 14 hectares of what is currently mostly paddocks. But the site is also in a green wedge area that is zoned for its environmental significance and is designated as bushfire prone. A creek running through the property has Aboriginal cultural heritage value. The terrain is hilly and accessible only by a narrow gravel road.



Sarah Hunter lives on Middle Hut Road, where she and her husband run a small egg farm more than a kilometre away from the proposed battery site. She was not informed of the project on Tuesday; she learned about it through a local chat group. Hunter said the battery system would industrialise the mostly agricultural area, characterised by its rolling hills and native wildlife, and used as a foraging area for the critically endangered swift parrot. “There is a place for batteries but not in the middle of a hilly area in the green wedge with a bushfire overlay,” she said. Related Article Opinion

Travel tips What happens when your EV runs low on a regional road trip? I found out Ben Groundwater Travel writer “It’s like a transformation of this beautiful area in the foothills of the Kinglake mountains. When you put in a big industrial site, that’s really damaging.”



Arthurs Creek resident Gareth Davies lives a few kilometres away, on a property at the foot of Mount Sugarloaf that came under direct attack on Black Saturday. “I just don’t think it’s the right place,” he said. “Everybody would say that, like it’s a NIMBY thing, but my concern is it’s a known bushfire-prone area. I could barely get insurance. I had to ring around like you wouldn’t believe to get insurance here because of the risk that the actuaries put on this area.” Middle Hut BESS is the first Victorian project for Turnbull Renewables, a company chaired by Malcolm Turnbull and founded by his wife, Lucy Turnbull. It has previously delivered two hydropower projects in NSW. Malcolm Turnbull told The Age the battery system would store excess wind and solar power generated during the day and dispatch it at night. “Storage is absolutely critical for the energy transition,” he said. “With more and more of our energy coming from wind and solar, and particularly solar storage, the ability to essentially time-shift electrons from the middle of a sunny day to the evening, is really vital.”



Former prime minister Malcolm Turnbull says the Middle Hut BESS will assist the energy transition. Dominic Lorrimer The former Coalition prime minister, who left politics in 2018, said the developers had reached out to the local community, and would host a public information session later this month. “We are confident that this is a good project. It’ll be good for all of us,” he said. Related Article Energy Renewables are slashing power prices, but energy chiefs fear it may not last The project is expected to be considered by Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny under the significant economic development provisions of the planning scheme.



A Victorian government spokesperson said the Department of Transport and Planning had not received an application for the project, and that all proposals were considered on their merits. “Green wedges play an important role in supporting agriculture, jobs, tourism and open space around Melbourne, which is why we are strengthening protections for them,” the spokesperson said. A Nillumbik Council spokesperson said they were aware of the proposal but it would not be assessed by council. “We believe the proposal will need to be publicly advertised, giving residents and other interested parties an opportunity to make a submission or object,” they said. According to Turnbull Renewables’ project timeline, construction would begin in 2028 and the battery would be operational by 2029.



A fire damaged Neoen Energy’s Victorian big battery project in July 2021. The fire burned for three days. A small handful of industrial-scale batteries have already been built around Melbourne’s fringes, including the Melbourne Renewable Energy Hub in Plumpton, Rangebank BESS in Cranbourne West and the Victorian Big Battery near Geelong. World.title: Police commissioner apologises for miscommunication after family told that deceased bushwalker was alive
World.content:
Updated NationalNSWTragedy Police commissioner apologises for miscommunication after family told that deceased bushwalker was alive Riley Walter and Jack Gramenz Updated August 20, 2026 — 7:49pm ,first published 11:47am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

NSW Police will investigate a series of failures that resulted in officers mistakenly informing the family of missing bushwalker Lily Hooper that the 18-year-old had been found alive after an eight-day search in the state’s Southern Highlands. Commissioner Mal Lanyon on Thursday was forced to apologise for the miscommunication that devastated her grieving parents, who, moments earlier, had celebrated what they believed was a miraculous survival. Loading Missing hiker Lily Hooper was found dead after an eight-day search in the NSW Southern Highlands. NSW Police For almost 20 minutes on Thursday, Hooper’s family believed she had been found alive in dense bushland before being told police were still working to determine her condition. Shortly after, police confirmed she had been found dead.



“I don’t know exactly what was said to her parents at the time, but obviously her condition, when she was located, the initial information that had been reported and was communicated, was that she was alive,” Lanyon said. NSW Police Commissioner said he apologised “unreservedly” for the miscommunication. KATE GERAGHTY A police officer at the search base, on the edge of the Nattai National Park, told Hooper’s parents, Jim and Kirrily Hooper, that the teenager was alive after an SES volunteer found her during a ground search. An elated Jim Hooper told reporters that he had never given up hope that his daughter would be found alive. On the eighth day of searching, he had laid a “charm” – his daughter’s guitar and a pack of Tim Tams – under the marquee the family had turned into a makeshift home since August 12. It was to beckon their daughter out of the bush. “She’s coming home,” he said through tears before loved ones celebrated at the search base.



“I’ve been beside myself ... we found her.” The miscommunication may have been sparked by a radio code believed to be used by SES searchers to report that a body has been found, in which they refer to full, half or empty water bottles to signal whether a person is alive in the event family members may be monitoring the radio. A half bottle of water is believed to indicate a person’s condition is unclear. Hooper’s mother said police had told her she was found alive with half a bottle of water in her possession. Police do not use the code during their own searches. Australian Army personnel who participated in the rescue operation are addressed on Thursday. Kate Geraghty “That miscommunication, I unashamedly apologise for any additional trauma that may have caused Lily’s family, but certainly for the embarrassment and confusion that caused,” Lanyon said, adding that police sought to correct the information at the earliest opportunity.



“The miscommunication, obviously, was born out of elation that Lily had been found and her condition at that time was such that searchers were relieved and certainly those at the command base were elated.” NSW SES Assistant Commissioner Colin Malone said information transmitted over radio communications could be broken up in remote areas. Lanyon on Thursday afternoon apologised to NSW Premier Chris Minns, who had earlier announced to a parliamentary budget estimates committee that Hooper was alive after he received the incorrect information. SES volunteers involved in the search for Lily Hooper. Kate Geraghty “I’ve got some terrible news, and I apologise to the committee. But it seems as if the early advice was wrong, and Lily’s body’s been found, and she’s been found deceased,” Minns said.



The information was passed from police to the premier via Police Minister Yasmin Catley, which Lanyon said was not unusual for a high-profile investigation. “The communication may have passed through a number of hands,” he said. “We will obviously look at that communication, how it took place, with a view to making sure we confirm that.” Lily Hooper began her hike on the Bonnum Pic Walking Trail on August 12. Kate Geraghty Lanyon had spoken to NSW SES Commissioner Mike Wassing and would review the failure, he said.



“This is not a circumstance I would like to see repeated,” Lanyon said. “What’s important now is we look at the communication between all agencies to make sure we improve it.” Almost 1000 searchers had scoured dense bush in the national park looking for Hooper since she was reported missing on August 12, having left her home in Sydney’s south-west that morning to hike the Bonnum Pic walking trail. The beginning of the trail. Kate Geraghty Police officers on horseback, motorcycles and from several units searched alongside Australian Defence Force personnel, NSW State Emergency Services volunteers and Rural Fire Service firefighters.



Helicopters and thermal imaging technology had also been used during the search for the teenager, who had remained in contact with her family on the day she went missing. Police found her Hyundai parked at the bottom of the challenging Bonnum Pic trail shortly after her family reported her missing. Emergency services gathering at the search site on Thursday. KATE GERAGHTY Authorities on Thursday evening were working to retrieve Hooper’s body from dense bush that Lanyon said could not be accessed via police helicopter. Her cause of death is yet to be determined and will be subject to a coronial investigation. Specialist officers were exploring the possibility of carrying Hooper’s body out of the bush, given the difficulty to access the site where she was found, which was not on a clear walking track, and was a significant distance from her car. It is unclear what injuries, if any, she sustained or when she died. The rescue operation combed through the Nattai National Park, south-west of Sydney. NSW State Emergency Service



“We’ll now work through a process, whether it’s manually, whether it’s on foot, to retrieve her body,” Lanyon said. “We’d like to bring her back to be with her family.” NSW Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane, who had earlier, citing media reports, posted on social media that the teenager had been found alive, said Hooper’s death was heartbreaking and an unimaginable loss. “So many people had been hoping for Lily’s safe return and today’s news will be difficult and deeply felt,” she said. Australian Army soldiers involved in the search on Thursday morning. KATE GERAGHTY



Federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, Hooper’s local member, published and then deleted a social media post indicating she had been found alive, later saying the incorrect reports of her survival made the family’s loss even worse. “We can only imagine what Lily’s family is going through right now. Such news would be a nightmare for any parent, and we grieve for Lily’s wider family,” Taylor told parliament. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the family’s loss was an unspeakable tragedy. “Lily Hooper had so much more to offer the world. Her passing, I have no doubt, will be felt very deeply,” he told parliament. “Our thoughts are of course with her family and loved ones on what is an incredibly sad and difficult day.”



MPs also rose for a moment’s silence. Wollondilly Shire Mayor Matt Gould said the council’s performing arts centre and library would be lit up in purple for the rest of the week in Hooper’s memory. Flags on the council chambers will be flown at half-mast. “They are small gestures, but I hope they help show in some way just how deeply Lily’s loss is being felt across our community, and how much Wollondilly is thinking of her family, friends and everyone who loved her,” Gould said.
